newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond new supply seen strong this week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond new supply seen strong this week.

text.p: The strong pace of new issuance of investment-grade and high-yield U.S. corporate bonds will show no signs of abating this week, syndicate officials said.
The primary market for junk bonds is expected to be particularly active, with 18 deals, totalling well over $3 billion in new supply, scheduled for this week, sources said.
In general, corporate issuers were attracted to continued strong demand for new supply from investors as well as low overall interest rate levels, they added.
Investors will have an large and diverse selection of new investment-grade securities to chose from this week including taxable municipal and Yankee bonds.
A $2.75 billion taxable municipal bond deal from the New Jersey Economic Development Authority is expected to draw considerable interest from corporate bond investors.
Proceeds from the deal, which is expected to set a record as the largest single municipal bond offering, will be used to fund the states' aggregate unfunded pension liability.
The offering will be underwritten by Merrill Lynch and is expected to include a significant amount of zero coupon bonds.

On Friday, the NJ State Treasurer announced the state has secured bids from bond insurance companies to insure the entire offering. As a result, the bonds will carry a AAA rating from the major rating agencies, he said.
Elsewhere, several Yankee bond offerings are also expected for this week.
British Aerospace Plc is expected to sell at least $600 million in 10-year and 30-year bonds in a private placement via J.P. Morgan Securities.
Norcen Energy Resources, a Canadian natural resouce company, is seen selling $250 million in five-year notes via Goldman Sachs & Co.
Among domestic issuers, Sears Roebuck Acceptance Corp is readying a global offering of $500 million in 10-year bonds via Goldman Sachs.
Also, SAFECO Corp is preparing a $500 million to $750 million trust preferred stock offering via Smith Barney Inc in a 144A private placement later this week.
On Monday morning, Standard & Poor's assigned a single-A rating to SAFECO's proposed trust preferred offering and cut the company's senior debt rating to A-plus from AA.
Proceeds from the deal will be used to finance the purchase of American States Financial Corp for $3.1 billion.
In the junk bond market, robust new issue activity is expected to get off to an early start with three deals seen pricing on Monday:

-Sinclair Broadcasting Group plans to sell $200 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes in a private placement via Smith Barney Inc, sources said. Price talk on the deal, which has not yet been rated, is in the nine percent area.

-Belden & Blake Corp, plans to sell $300 million in 144A 10-year senior subordinated notes via Chase Securities Inc. Price talk for the deal, rated B3/B-minus, is 9.625 percent to 9.875 percent. The company is in the oil and gas exploration and production business.

-DI Industries Inc is expected to price $125 million in 10-year senior notes via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. Price talk on the notes, rated B1/B-plus, is in the nine percent area. DI is the second largest U.S. onshore oil and gas contract driller.
